previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with somnolence and a history of his left nephrostomy tube falling out multiple times, which he reinserted non-sterilely using duct tape. He presented with systemic signs of infection, including elevated white blood cell count and CRP, and impaired kidney function. Imaging confirmed appropriate tube positioning after replacement by interventional radiology. He was started on a 10-day course of IV meropenem for a suspected complicated urinary tract infection. His inflammatory markers and renal function improved during the hospitalization. However, he left against medical advice on the fourth day of treatment despite warnings about risks of incomplete therapy. Discharge instructions emphasized urgent follow-up with urology and infectious disease, continuation of home medications, and avoidance of self-reinsertion of the nephrostomy tube.
